guide.what: Conjunctions are linking words like y, pero, porque and cuando that join words or whole sentences. Many of them decide the verb mood that follows: some always need the subjunctive.

rules.d: These always take the subjunctive because the action is not real yet: para que, antes de que, sin que, a menos que, a no ser que, con tal de que, en caso de que, a fin de que, siempre y cuando.
rules.ex: Te llamo antes de que salgas.
rules.exEn: I'll call you before you leave.

rules.t: Time words: subjunctive for the future
rules.d: Cuando, hasta que, en cuanto, tan pronto como, después de que and apenas take the subjunctive when the action hasn't happened yet, and the indicative for habits or the past.
rules.ex: Cuando llegue a Panamá, te escribo. / Cuando llegué, te escribí.
rules.exEn: When I get to Panama, I'll write to you. / When I arrived, I wrote to you.

rules.d: Aunque + indicative states a fact (although). Aunque + subjunctive presents a possibility or something you dismiss (even if).
rules.ex: Aunque hace calor, voy a correr. / Aunque haga calor, voy a correr.
rules.exEn: Although it's hot, I'm going running. / Even if it's hot, I'm going running.

rules.d: Use present indicative for real conditions and imperfect subjunctive for unreal ones. 'Si tenga' is always wrong.
rules.ex: Si tengo tiempo, voy. / Si tuviera tiempo, iría.
rules.exEn: If I have time, I'll go. / If I had time, I would go.

rules.d: With para, antes de, después de, sin: if both parts have the same subject, drop 'que' and use the infinitive.
rules.ex: Estudio para aprobar. / Estudio para que mi hijo se sienta orgulloso.
rules.exEn: I study to pass. / I study so that my son feels proud.

rules.d: Y becomes e before the sound i (i-, hi-): padre e hijo. O becomes u before the sound o (o-, ho-): siete u ocho. Not before hie-: agua y hielo.
rules.ex: Busco a alguien honesto e inteligente, ayer u hoy.
rules.exEn: I'm looking for someone honest and intelligent, yesterday or today.

rules.d: Pero adds a contrast. Sino corrects a negative: no A sino B. Before a conjugated verb use sino que.
rules.ex: No es caro, pero no lo necesito. / No es caro sino barato.
rules.exEn: It's not expensive, but I don't need it. / It's not expensive but cheap.

rules.t: Porque, por qué, el porqué, por que
rules.d: Porque = because. ¿Por qué? = why (questions, direct or indirect). El porqué = the reason (noun). Por que (rare) = for which: la razón por (la) que.
rules.exEn: Why didn't you come? —Because I was sick.

rules.d: At the start of a sentence, como gives the cause ('since'). Porque usually goes after the main idea and doesn't start a sentence in this way.
rules.ex: Como no había luz, cenamos con velas.
rules.exEn: Since there was no power, we had dinner by candlelight.

mistakes.why: Cuando about the future needs the subjunctive.
Si never takes the present subjunctive.
Same subject: para + infinitive. Para que always needs subjunctive.

mistakes.wrong: No es mi hermano pero mi primo.
mistakes.right: No es mi hermano sino mi primo.

mistakes.wrong: Hablo español y inglés y italiano.
mistakes.why: Y becomes e before i-; also use commas in lists.

mistakes.wrong: No fui por qué estaba cansado.
mistakes.why: Because is porque (one word, no accent).

items.use: Joins words or sentences. Becomes 'e' before words starting with the sound i- (i-, hi-): padres e hijos.
items.ex: Compré arroz y frijoles.
items.exEn: I bought rice and beans.

items.use: Introduces a clause: creo que..., quiero que + subjunctive. Never drop it like English 'that'. In comparisons it means 'than': más alto que yo.
items.ex: Creo que va a llover esta tarde.
items.exEn: I think (that) it's going to rain this afternoon.

items.use: Offers a choice. Becomes 'u' before o- or ho-: siete u ocho. Between numbers it is written without an accent today: 3 o 4.
items.ex: ¿Quieres café o jugo?
items.exEn: Do you want coffee or juice?

items.use: Adds a contrast to what came before. If the first part is negative and you correct it, use 'sino' instead.
items.ex: Es caro, pero vale la pena.
items.exEn: It's expensive, but it's worth it.

items.use: Real conditions use the indicative: si llueve, me quedo. Never use present subjunctive after si. Unreal conditions use the imperfect subjunctive: si tuviera dinero... No accent (sí = yes).
items.ex: Si llueve, nos quedamos en casa.
items.exEn: If it rains, we'll stay home.

items.use: At the start of a sentence it means 'since' (cause): Como no viniste, me fui. In the middle it means 'as/like'. With subjunctive it can be a threat: como llegues tarde...
items.ex: Como no tenía carro, tomé un taxi.
items.exEn: Since I didn't have a car, I took a taxi.

items.use: Gives a reason, usually after the main idea. One word, no accent. '¿Por qué?' (two words, accent) asks why; 'el porqué' means the reason.
items.ex: No fui a la fiesta porque estaba cansado.
items.exEn: I didn't go to the party because I was tired.

items.use: Indicative for habits or the past: cuando llego, como. Subjunctive for the future: cuando llegues, llámame. No accent unless it's a question (¿cuándo?).
items.ex: Cuando llegues a casa, mándame un mensaje.
items.exEn: When you get home, send me a message.

items.use: Joins negative ideas: no como carne ni pescado. 'Ni' alone can mean 'not even': ni idea.
items.ex: No tengo tiempo ni ganas.
items.exEn: I have neither time nor desire.

items.use: Indicative for a known fact (aunque llueve = although it's raining). Subjunctive for a possibility or 'even if' (aunque llueva = even if it rains).
items.ex: Aunque llueva, vamos a la playa.
items.exEn: Even if it rains, we're going to the beach.

items.use: Replaces 'y' before words starting with the sound i: español e inglés, madre e hija. Not before hie- or hia-: agua y hielo.
items.ex: Hablo español e inglés.
items.exEn: I speak Spanish and English.

items.use: At the start, a filler like 'well': pues, no sé. Between clauses it gives a cause (formal) or a consequence.
items.ex: No pude ir, pues estaba enfermo.
items.exEn: I couldn't go, since I was sick.
items.latam: Panamanians often say 'pues' as a filler at the end of phrases.

items.use: With indicative it means 'while': mientras cocino, escucho música. With subjunctive it means 'as long as': mientras no llueva.
items.ex: Mientras cocino, escucho música.
items.exEn: While I cook, I listen to music.

items.use: Corrects a negative statement: no A sino B. Use 'sino que' before a full clause with a verb. Don't confuse with 'si no' (if not).
items.ex: No es panameño sino colombiano.
items.exEn: He isn't Panamanian but Colombian.

items.use: Introduces a result, very common in speech. Takes the indicative.
items.ex: Estaba cansado, así que me acosté temprano.
items.exEn: I was tired, so I went to bed early.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive. If the subject is the same, use 'para' + infinitive instead.
items.ex: Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.
items.exEn: I'm explaining it so that you understand it.

items.use: Shows a consequence or the next step. Very common in Latin American speech to link ideas.
items.ex: No había bus, entonces caminé.
items.exEn: There was no bus, so I walked.
items.latam: Used constantly in LatAm conversation as 'so'.

items.use: Replaces 'o' before words starting with the sound o: siete u ocho, mujer u hombre.
items.ex: ¿Necesitas siete u ocho sillas?
items.exEn: Do you need seven or eight chairs?

items.use: Gives a known reason, often at the start of the sentence. Indicative.
items.ex: Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame con esto.
items.exEn: Since you're here, help me with this.

items.use: Rephrases or clarifies, extremely common in speech. More casual than 'es decir'.
items.ex: Llego el lunes, o sea, en tres días.
items.exEn: I'm arriving Monday, I mean, in three days.

items.use: Points back to a reason already said. Indicative.
items.ex: Llovió mucho; por eso no salimos.
items.exEn: It rained a lot; that's why we didn't go out.

items.use: Subjunctive when the event is still in the future: espera hasta que llegue. Indicative for the past: esperé hasta que llegó.
items.ex: Espérame aquí hasta que vuelva.
items.exEn: Wait for me here until I come back.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive. If the subject is the same, use 'antes de' + infinitive.
items.ex: Vámonos antes de que empiece a llover.
items.exEn: Let's go before it starts raining.

items.use: Subjunctive for the future, indicative for the past. With the same subject, prefer 'después de' + infinitive.
items.ex: Te llamo después de que termine la reunión.
items.exEn: I'll call you after the meeting ends.

items.use: Strong contrast, usually at the start of a sentence followed by a comma. Common in writing.
items.ex: Estudió mucho; sin embargo, no aprobó.
items.exEn: He studied a lot; however, he didn't pass.

items.use: Explains or rephrases, more formal than 'o sea'. Good for DELE writing.
items.ex: Vivo en el interior, es decir, fuera de la capital.
items.exEn: I live in the interior, that is, outside the capital.
items.latam: In Panama 'el interior' means the provinces outside Panama City.

items.use: Formal consequence, very useful in essays.
items.ex: No tengo visa; por lo tanto, no puedo viajar.
items.exEn: I don't have a visa; therefore, I can't travel.

items.use: Contrasts two facts. Indicative.
items.ex: Yo prefiero la playa, mientras que mi esposa prefiere la montaña.
items.exEn: I prefer the beach, whereas my wife prefers the mountains.

items.use: From a moment in the past until now. Indicative.
items.ex: Desde que vivo en Panamá, hablo más español.
items.exEn: Since I've lived in Panama, I speak more Spanish.

items.use: Joins two equal elements: tanto los niños como los adultos.
items.ex: Tanto los niños como los adultos disfrutaron el show.
items.exEn: Both the kids and the adults enjoyed the show.

items.use: Two negatives. If the verb comes after, add no before it: no tengo ni... ni....
items.ex: No me gusta ni el café ni el té.
items.exEn: I like neither coffee nor tea.

items.use: Presents two options that exclude each other.
items.ex: O pagas ahora o pierdes la reserva.
items.exEn: Either you pay now or you lose the booking.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive. If the subject is the same, use 'sin' + infinitive.
items.ex: Salió sin que nadie lo viera.
items.exEn: He left without anyone seeing him.

items.use: Subjunctive for the future: en cuanto llegue. Indicative for habits or the past. Not the same as 'en cuanto a' (as for).
items.ex: En cuanto sepa algo, te aviso.
items.exEn: As soon as I know something, I'll let you know.

items.en: even though, despite the fact that
items.use: Indicative for facts; subjunctive when the fact is hypothetical or already known and not important.
items.ex: Salimos a pesar de que estaba lloviendo.
items.exEn: We went out even though it was raining.

items.use: With indicative = whenever (habit). With subjunctive = provided that (condition).
items.ex: Puedes usar mi carro siempre que lo cuides.
items.exEn: You can use my car provided that you take care of it.

items.use: Use instead of 'sino' when a conjugated verb follows: no solo... sino que....
items.ex: No me llamó, sino que me escribió.
items.exEn: He didn't call me; rather, he wrote to me.

items.use: Adds a second, often stronger idea. With a verb: no solo... sino que también.
items.ex: Habla no solo español sino también portugués.
items.exEn: She speaks not only Spanish but also Portuguese.

items.use: Always takes the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive: como si fuera, como si hubiera visto.
items.ex: Habla como si fuera el jefe.
items.exEn: He talks as if he were the boss.

items.use: With indicative = so (result). With subjunctive = so that (purpose).
items.ex: Habla más alto, de modo que todos te oigan.
items.exEn: Speak louder so that everyone hears you.

items.use: Same as 'de modo que'. Indicative for result, subjunctive for purpose.
items.ex: No había nadie, de manera que me fui.
items.exEn: There was nobody there, so I left.

items.use: Formal cause, common in writing. Indicative.
items.ex: Puesto que no hay quórum, se suspende la reunión.
items.exEn: Since there's no quorum, the meeting is suspended.

items.use: Formal cause, often at the start. Indicative.
items.ex: Dado que es feriado, los bancos están cerrados.
items.exEn: Given that it's a holiday, the banks are closed.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive.
items.ex: En caso de que llueva, llevamos paraguas.
items.exEn: In case it rains, we'll take umbrellas.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive.
items.ex: No voy a ir a menos que me invites.
items.exEn: I'm not going unless you invite me.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive.
items.ex: Te presto el carro con tal de que lo devuelvas mañana.
items.exEn: I'll lend you the car as long as you return it tomorrow.

items.use: Subjunctive for the future, indicative for the past or habits.
items.ex: Tan pronto como llegue, te llamo.
items.exEn: As soon as I arrive, I'll call you.

items.use: Subjunctive for the future, indicative for the past.
items.ex: Una vez que termines, puedes irte.
items.exEn: Once you finish, you can leave.

items.use: Usually indicative because it describes habits.
items.ex: Cada vez que voy al centro, hay tranque.
items.exEn: Every time I go downtown, there's a traffic jam.

items.use: As a conjunction, 'as soon as'. Subjunctive for the future. Very common in Latin America.
items.ex: Apenas llegues, avísame.
items.exEn: As soon as you arrive, let me know.
items.latam: Much more common in LatAm than in Spain with this meaning.

items.use: Adds elements in formal style: el inglés así como el francés. Also 'just as' in comparisons.
items.ex: Ofrecemos clases de inglés, así como de francés.
items.exEn: We offer English classes, as well as French.

items.use: Formal 'however', very common in DELE writing.
items.ex: El plan es bueno; no obstante, es muy caro.
items.exEn: The plan is good; nevertheless, it's very expensive.

items.use: Links a cause to its result in the same sentence. Indicative.
items.ex: Perdí el bus, por lo que llegué tarde.
items.exEn: I missed the bus, so I arrived late.

items.en: because, due to the fact that
items.use: Formal cause, common in news and reports.
items.ex: El vuelo se canceló debido a que había tormenta.
items.exEn: The flight was canceled because there was a storm.

items.use: Formal concession, always indicative.
items.ex: Si bien es caro, la calidad es excelente.
items.exEn: Although it's expensive, the quality is excellent.

items.use: Subjunctive for any amount (por más que estudies); indicative for a real fact.
items.ex: Por más que lo intento, no me sale.
items.exEn: No matter how hard I try, I can't do it.

items.use: Formal 'even if'. Subjunctive for hypotheses. Note: aun without accent here.
items.ex: Aun cuando llueva, el evento se realizará.
items.exEn: Even if it rains, the event will take place.

items.use: Two things change together. Subjunctive for the future.
items.ex: A medida que practicas, hablas con más confianza.
items.exEn: As you practice, you speak with more confidence.

items.use: Followed by indicative (or imperfect subjunctive), never present subjunctive: por si llueve. 'Por si acaso' = just in case.
items.ex: Lleva una sombrilla por si llueve.
items.exEn: Take an umbrella in case it rains.

items.use: Presents options; ya sea is fixed: ya sea en carro o en bus.
items.ex: Puedes pagar ya sea en efectivo o con tarjeta.
items.exEn: You can pay either in cash or by card.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive. Stronger than 'siempre que'.
items.ex: Puedes salir, siempre y cuando vuelvas antes de las diez.
items.exEn: You can go out as long as you're back before ten.

items.use: Same as 'por lo tanto', slightly more formal.
items.ex: Es menor de edad y, por tanto, no puede votar.
items.exEn: He's a minor and therefore can't vote.

items.use: Same as 'de modo que'. Indicative = result, subjunctive = purpose.
items.ex: Organiza la reunión de forma que todos puedan asistir.
items.exEn: Organize the meeting so that everyone can attend.

items.use: Formal consequence, used in writing and speeches.
items.ex: Subieron los costos y, por consiguiente, los precios.
items.exEn: Costs went up and, consequently, so did prices.

items.use: Tan + adjective/adverb + que + result: tan cansado que...
items.ex: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí en el bus.
items.exEn: I was so tired that I fell asleep on the bus.

items.use: Verb + tanto que + result. Tanto/a/os/as + noun + que also works.
items.ex: Comió tanto que le dolió la barriga.
items.exEn: He ate so much that his stomach hurt.

items.use: Emphatic negative. Before the verb, no 'no' is needed: ni siquiera me saludó.
items.ex: Ni siquiera me dijo adiós.
items.exEn: He didn't even say goodbye to me.

items.use: Compares or adds: al igual que tú, yo también...
items.ex: Al igual que tú, yo también extraño a mi familia.
items.exEn: Just like you, I miss my family too.

items.use: Shows a match with how something was said or done. 'Tal y como' is a common variant.
items.ex: Lo hice tal como me dijiste.
items.exEn: I did it just as you told me.

items.use: Compares two equal things: es igual que su papá.
items.ex: Ella cocina igual que su abuela.
items.exEn: She cooks just like her grandmother.

items.use: Comparison of superiority. Before numbers use 'más de': más de diez.
items.ex: Panamá es más caliente que Nueva York.
items.exEn: Panama is hotter than New York.

items.use: Comparison of equality with adjectives and adverbs. With nouns use tanto/a/os/as… como.
items.ex: Mi hijo es tan alto como yo.
items.exEn: My son is as tall as I am.

items.use: Like 'por más que'. Subjunctive for hypothetical amounts.
items.ex: Por mucho que insistas, no voy a cambiar de idea.
items.exEn: However much you insist, I won't change my mind.

items.use: Always takes the subjunctive. Same as 'a menos que'.
items.ex: Iremos a la playa, a no ser que llueva.
items.exEn: We'll go to the beach, unless it rains.

items.use: Same as 'después de que', very common in Latin American news. Subjunctive for the future.
items.ex: Luego de que se fue, todos se relajaron.
items.exEn: After he left, everyone relaxed.
items.latam: More common in LatAm than in Spain.

items.use: Takes the indicative (never present subjunctive, like 'si'). Imperfect subjunctive for unlikely cases.
items.ex: Incluso si llueve, el partido sigue.
items.exEn: Even if it rains, the game goes on.

items.use: Like 'incluso si'. Indicative or imperfect subjunctive. 'Aun' without accent = even.
items.ex: Aun si me pagaran el doble, no me mudaría.
items.exEn: Even if they paid me double, I wouldn't move.

items.use: Formal synonym of 'a pesar de que', common in news.
items.ex: Pese a que estaba enfermo, fue a trabajar.
items.exEn: Despite being sick, he went to work.

items.en: in view of the fact that
items.use: Formal cause based on a visible fact. Indicative.
items.ex: En vista de que nadie vino, cancelamos la clase.
items.exEn: Seeing that nobody came, we canceled the class.

items.use: Positive cause with a full clause. Indicative.
items.ex: Llegamos a tiempo gracias a que no había tráfico.
items.exEn: We arrived on time thanks to there being no traffic.

items.use: Formal 'para que'. Always takes the subjunctive.
items.ex: Le enviamos el formulario a fin de que lo complete.
items.exEn: We're sending you the form so that you can complete it.

items.use: Common way to give an excuse or explanation in speech.
items.ex: Perdón por llegar tarde, es que había mucho tranque.
items.exEn: Sorry I'm late, it's just that there was a lot of traffic.

items.use: Cause linked to a new situation. Indicative.
items.ex: Ahora que tienes carro, puedes visitarnos más.
items.exEn: Now that you have a car, you can visit us more.

items.use: Formal and written. Very common in LatAm academic and legal texts.
items.ex: Hubo errores y, por ende, se repitió la votación.
items.exEn: There were errors and therefore the vote was repeated.

items.use: Introduces a consequence and normally takes the subjunctive (a surprise for learners).
items.ex: Llovió toda la semana; de ahí que el río esté crecido.
items.exEn: It rained all week; hence the river is high.

items.use: Cause with a full clause; less common than 'porque' or 'debido a que'.
items.ex: Se retrasó a causa de que el puente estaba cerrado.
items.exEn: He was delayed because the bridge was closed.

items.use: Like 'a medida que'. Subjunctive for the future.
items.ex: Conforme pasan los días, me siento mejor.
items.exEn: As the days go by, I feel better.

items.use: As a conjunction: 'as' (según iban llegando) or 'depending on' (según lo que digas).
items.ex: Según iban llegando, los invitados se sentaban.
items.exEn: As they arrived, the guests sat down.

items.use: Formal purpose with a different subject. Always subjunctive.
items.ex: Ahorramos con el fin de que nuestros hijos estudien.
items.exEn: We save so that our children can study.

items.use: Formal condition, always subjunctive.
items.ex: Firmo a condición de que cambien la cláusula.
items.exEn: I'll sign on condition that you change the clause.

items.use: As 'unless' it takes the subjunctive; as 'except that' it takes the indicative.
items.ex: Nos vemos el sábado, salvo que llueva.
items.exEn: See you on Saturday, unless it rains.

items.use: Indicative for a fact ('except that'), subjunctive for a condition ('unless').
items.ex: Todo salió bien, excepto que perdí mis lentes.
items.exEn: Everything went well, except that I lost my glasses.

items.use: Formal alternatives, often in instructions.
items.ex: Puede pagar bien en efectivo, bien con tarjeta.
items.exEn: You can pay either in cash or by card.

items.use: Literary alternation: ya alegre, ya triste.
items.ex: Ya reía, ya lloraba, sin saber por qué.
items.exEn: Now she laughed, now she cried, without knowing why.

items.use: Formal choice between options.
items.ex: Sea por dinero, sea por amor, se casó.
items.exEn: Whether for money or for love, he got married.

items.use: Slightly more formal 'o', often at the start of the second option.
items.ex: Puede llamarnos o bien escribirnos un correo.
items.exEn: You can call us or alternatively send us an email.

items.use: Two things grow together. Subjunctive for the future: cuanto más practiques, más aprenderás.
items.ex: Cuanto más practico, más fácil me resulta.
items.exEn: The more I practice, the easier it gets.

items.use: Latin American form of 'cuanto más… más'.
items.ex: Mientras más leas, mejor vas a escribir.
items.exEn: The more you read, the better you'll write.
items.latam: Very common in LatAm; Spain prefers 'cuanto más… más'.

items.use: Caribbean and Central American colloquial: 'while' or 'by the time'. Often subjunctive for the future.
items.ex: Espérame en lo que me baño.
items.exEn: Wait for me while I take a shower.
items.latam: Typical in Panama and the Caribbean; less used in Spain.

items.use: Latin American 'as soon as'. Subjunctive for the future.
items.ex: Ni bien llegó, se puso a trabajar.
items.exEn: As soon as he arrived, he started working.
items.latam: Mostly used in Southern Cone and parts of LatAm.

items.use: Cause based on what is clear. Indicative.
items.ex: Visto que no contestas, te escribo.
items.exEn: Seeing that you don't answer, I'm writing to you.

items.use: Indicative = result; subjunctive = purpose.
items.ex: Lo explicó de tal manera que todos lo entendimos.
items.exEn: He explained it in such a way that we all understood.

items.use: Formal consequence for writing.
items.ex: No pagó la cuota; en consecuencia, perdió la membresía.
items.exEn: He didn't pay the fee; consequently, he lost the membership.

items.use: Formal conclusion, often after summarizing.
items.ex: Así pues, la reunión queda para el lunes.
items.exEn: So, the meeting is set for Monday.

items.use: Formal or philosophical 'therefore': pienso, luego existo. Normally 'luego' is an adverb meaning 'later'.
items.ex: Pienso, luego existo.
items.exEn: I think, therefore I am.

items.use: Colloquial consequence, often in warnings or surprise. One word; 'con que' (two words) means 'as long as'.
items.ex: Ya es tarde, conque apúrate.
items.exEn: It's late already, so hurry up.

items.en: while, at the same time as
items.use: Formal simultaneity.
items.ex: Sonreía al tiempo que firmaba el contrato.
items.exEn: He smiled as he signed the contract.

items.use: The pattern behind 'sino': deny A, affirm B.
items.ex: No quiero té sino café.
items.exEn: I don't want tea but coffee.

items.use: Draws a conclusion in conversation.
items.ex: No tienes efectivo, o sea que pagamos con tarjeta.
items.exEn: You don't have cash, so we'll pay by card.

items.use: Formal 'es decir', used in writing.
items.ex: Llegará en breve, esto es, en cinco minutos.
items.exEn: He'll arrive shortly, that is, in five minutes.

items.use: Colloquial: adds a surprising fact. Indicative.
items.ex: Aprobó, y eso que no estudió nada.
items.exEn: He passed, even though he didn't study at all.

items.use: After verbs of movement (venir, ir, salir) with a different subject. Subjunctive.
items.ex: Vengo a que me expliques la tarea.
items.exEn: I've come so that you can explain the homework to me.

items.use: Purpose to avoid a risk. Always subjunctive.
items.ex: Lleva abrigo, no sea que te resfríes.
items.exEn: Take a jacket, in case you catch a cold.

items.use: Colloquial version of 'no sea que'. Subjunctive.
items.ex: Llama antes, no vaya a ser que esté cerrado.
items.exEn: Call first, in case it's closed.

items.use: Negative cause with a full clause. Indicative.
items.ex: Llegamos tarde por culpa de que se dañó el carro.
items.exEn: We got there late because the car broke down.

items.use: Por muy + adjective/adverb + que + subjunctive usually.
items.ex: Por muy cansado que estés, termina el trabajo.
items.exEn: However tired you are, finish the work.

items.use: Hypothesis, usually with subjunctive.
items.ex: Suponiendo que llegue a tiempo, empezamos a las ocho.
items.exEn: Assuming he arrives on time, we'll start at eight.

items.use: Two words: a minimal condition. Subjunctive. Don't confuse with 'conque' (so).
items.ex: Con que me avises antes, está bien.
items.exEn: As long as you let me know beforehand, it's fine.

items.use: Formal comparison of manner.
items.ex: Lo hice de la misma manera que tú.
items.exEn: I did it the same way you did.

items.use: Same as 'de la misma manera que'.
items.ex: Del mismo modo que cuidas tu salud, cuida tu dinero.
items.exEn: Just as you look after your health, look after your money.

items.use: Equal comparison: pedí lo mismo que tú.
items.ex: Quiero lo mismo que pediste tú.
items.exEn: I want the same thing you ordered.

items.use: Comparison of inferiority. Before numbers use 'menos de'.
items.ex: Este celular es menos caro que el otro.
items.exEn: This cell phone is less expensive than the other one.

items.use: Fuller form of 'en caso de que'. Always subjunctive.
items.ex: En el caso de que no pueda venir, le aviso.
items.exEn: In the event that I can't come, I'll let you know.

items.use: Formal purpose, subjunctive. Good for DELE essays.
items.ex: Creamos el programa con el objetivo de que más jóvenes estudien.
items.exEn: We created the program so that more young people study.

items.use: Colloquial: wraps up a story.
items.ex: Total que no llegamos a tiempo.
items.exEn: So in the end we didn't make it on time.

items.use: Formal: doing something despite knowing. Indicative.
items.ex: Lo hizo a sabiendas de que estaba prohibido.
items.exEn: He did it knowing full well it was forbidden.

items.use: Legal and formal cause.
items.ex: Se rechaza la solicitud, toda vez que está incompleta.
items.exEn: The application is rejected, since it is incomplete.

items.use: Very formal cause used in reports.
items.ex: Habida cuenta de que no hay fondos, se pospone la obra.
items.exEn: Bearing in mind there are no funds, the work is postponed.

items.use: Introduces a qualification or objection, formal.
items.ex: Puedes ir; ahora bien, vuelve temprano.
items.exEn: You can go; however, come back early.

items.use: Formal: 'while' (simultaneity) or 'as' (in the role of).
items.ex: En tanto que el jefe hablaba, todos tomaban notas.
items.exEn: While the boss was speaking, everyone took notes.

items.use: Formal and legal 'until'. Subjunctive. Often 'hasta tanto (no)'.
items.ex: No se pagará hasta tanto se entregue la obra.
items.exEn: No payment will be made until the work is delivered.

items.use: Literary 'as soon as'.
items.ex: No bien salió el sol, empezamos a caminar.
items.exEn: As soon as the sun came up, we started walking.

items.use: Literary result or purpose.
items.ex: Llegó temprano, de suerte que consiguió asiento.
items.exEn: He arrived early, so he got a seat.

items.use: Formal: introduces a list.
items.ex: Hay tres requisitos, a saber: pasaporte, foto y pago.
items.exEn: There are three requirements, namely: passport, photo and payment.

items.use: Literary 'pero', no accent (más = more).
items.ex: Quiso hablar, mas no encontró las palabras.
items.exEn: He wanted to speak, but he couldn't find the words.

items.use: Archaic and literary alternation.
items.ex: Ora cantaba, ora lloraba.
items.exEn: Now she sang, now she wept.

items.use: Old-fashioned formal cause, or 'however/whatever way' with subjunctive.
items.ex: Como quiera que lo hagas, hazlo bien.
items.exEn: However you do it, do it well.

items.use: Concession with a small amount. Subjunctive.
items.ex: Por poco que ganes, ahorra algo.
items.exEn: However little you earn, save something.

items.use: Latin American colloquial 'even if' + subjunctive: así llueva, voy.
items.ex: Voy a ir, así tenga que caminar.
items.exEn: I'm going, even if I have to walk.
items.latam: Common in LatAm (Panama, Colombia, Venezuela); rare in Spain.

items.use: Two words: 'if not' or 'otherwise'. Don't confuse with 'sino' (but rather).
items.ex: Apúrate; si no, perdemos el bus.
items.exEn: Hurry up; otherwise we'll miss the bus.

items.use: Adds another reason or fact. Indicative.
items.ex: Es buen trabajo, además de que queda cerca.
items.exEn: It's a good job, besides the fact that it's close by.

items.use: Like 'además de que', adds information.
items.ex: Aparte de que es caro, el servicio es malo.
items.exEn: Apart from it being expensive, the service is bad.

items.en: insofar as, to the extent that
items.use: Formal condition or degree. Indicative for facts, subjunctive for the future.
items.ex: Te ayudaré en la medida en que pueda.
items.exEn: I'll help you as much as I can.

items.use: Preference: prefiero X antes que Y. Also 'before' in formal style.
items.ex: Prefiero caminar antes que manejar en ese tráfico.
items.exEn: I'd rather walk than drive in that traffic.

items.use: Formal cause in legal or academic texts.
items.ex: Es importante, por cuanto afecta a todos.
items.exEn: It's important, inasmuch as it affects everyone.

items.w: o lo que es lo mismo
items.use: Emphatic rephrasing, good for essays.
items.ex: Gastó el doble, o lo que es lo mismo, perdió dinero.
items.exEn: He spent double, or in other words, lost money.

items.use: Purpose with a different subject. Subjunctive.
items.ex: Le escribí con la intención de que me respondiera.
items.exEn: I wrote to him hoping he would answer.

items.use: Colloquial Latin American form of 'cuanto más… más'.
items.ex: Entre más duermo, más sueño tengo.
items.exEn: The more I sleep, the sleepier I am.
items.latam: Heard in Central America and Mexico; avoid in formal writing.

items.use: Tanto/a/os/as + noun + que + result.
items.ex: Tenía tanta hambre que me comí dos platos.
items.exEn: I was so hungry that I ate two plates.

items.use: 'More than' with verbs (trabaja más que yo); after a negative, 'nothing but' (no hace más que quejarse).
items.ex: No hace más que quejarse.
items.exEn: He does nothing but complain.
